posts.author: Haekraal
posts.body: Hello, I'm wondering if there's a plugin or something I can do in-game that would allow the player to customize their resolution abiding by the base aspect ratio of 16:9 in the option screen, or something similar? Thanks!

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
This is going to cause problems you might not have accounted for.
The assets are not vector graphics. They cannot be scaled infinitely like you might be familiar with in most 3D games or other 2D engines that allow for vector graphics.
When you increase the resolution, you are increasing the number of pixels shown on screen. This means that as the resolution increases (on the same sized monitor) it will look like everything else is getting smaller. Also, your camera will begin to see more and more of the map.
And this could cause problems with both the engine and/or game play mechanics, so I suggest avoiding this.
If you are still interested in the plugin, then hopefully someone can provide it for you. Unfortunately I am not aware of any.

Is there any way to maintain the quality of graphics regardless of the screen's resolution, since my game is very asset-heavy? Regardless, thank you for your thorough answer

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Haekraal said:
Is there any way to maintain the quality of graphics regardless of the screen's resolution
Click to expand...
Not while making the graphics take up a proportional amount of space in the window.
You can resize the game window in your System 2 tab, which does not affect the resolution - it merely increases how much of the map is visible to the player.
What you may not realize is that traditional video games that offer a choice of resolution in the menu do one of several possible things:
1 - They actually resize the game window, as described above, so the game looks smaller on larger monitors
2 - They use vector graphics and models as
@TheAM-Dol
described above
3 - Or they have actual different sets of artwork drawn to look good at different sizes, and changing the game's resolution also changes which assets are loaded
Number 3 is technically possible in RPG Maker, but it would be a lot of work. Most people simply choose a window size that they want to design their game and graphics around, and if a player decides to adjust that manually on their system, then they do.
There is this post that has code (you would paste it into a text editor, save as a *.js file, include as a plugin):
That will make it so if a player
does
adjust their window manually, via the maximize or fullscreen buttons, it won't scale your graphics unless their screen is large enough to smoothly double what you have drawn.
